use_when: a justified Task Pod requires multi-role DAG/resume execution that the current host cannot provide adequately
AAOP can delegate one bounded outcome while retaining Working Contract, Journey, authorization, acceptance, and handoff ownership
avoid_when: host-native subagents or sequential role isolation are sufficient
the task is small enough for one agent
the provider would become a second top-level orchestration state machine beside AAOP
the user would have to operate YAML, DAG dependencies, or role selection manually

minimal_commands: review current upstream installation instructions and exact release/revision
install only when a proven Task Pod execution capability gap remains
delegate one bounded Pod rather than the whole AAOP Journey
notes: Prefer host-native multi-agent primitives before adding this provider.
If selected, map AAOP Pod members/acceptance criteria into the provider execution surface while keeping AAOP as the authoritative control plane.
Use provider human_input/approval primitives only to surface questions/approvals already justified by AAOP Decision Ownership and Autonomy Policy.
Capture the provider revision and bounded delegated Pod definition for consequential use.

permissions: provider installation/configuration permissions appropriate to the selected host
only the tools/credentials required by the delegated Task Pod
no automatic widening of repository, production, billing, or secret access

checks: confirm AAOP still owns the Working Contract and Journey state
confirm no delegated workflow exceeds five Task Pod members/responsibility contexts
confirm human_input/approval steps correspond to real human-owned/authorization gates rather than routine engineering questions
confirm the provider returns evidence and outputs to the AAOP accountable owner
confirm the Pod acceptance criteria pass before handoff

steps: preserve completed evidence/handoff artifacts needed for continuity
remove only provider-specific configuration/dependencies introduced for this adoption
fall back to host-native or sequential role isolation without changing the Working Contract goal

warnings: Do not run a provider DAG and AAOP Journey as competing sources of truth.
Provider resume state is execution detail; AAOP Working Contract/Journey remain authoritative continuity boundaries.
A provider cannot bypass missing credentials, network restrictions, unresolved human-owned decisions, or production authorization.
